data.title: Miconazole 2% cream
data.body:
_Topicals · I Antifungals — Azoles_

**Class:** Imidazole antifungal

## Mechanism of action
- Inhibits 14-α-demethylase; at higher concentrations directly damages membranes
- Also active against Gram-positive bacteria

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Cutaneous and mucosal candidiasis (cream, oral gel, vaginal)
- Tinea corporis/cruris/pedis, pityriasis versicolor, angular cheilitis (Candida/staph)
- Napkin candidiasis

## Dose & formulations
- Cream 2%: twice daily, continue 10–14 days after lesions clear
- Oral gel: 4 times daily after food (oral thrush)

## Adverse effects
- Local irritation, contact dermatitis

## Contraindications
- Oral gel in infants under 4–6 months (choking risk)
- Oral gel with warfarin (see interactions)

## Drug interactions
- Miconazole oral gel (and even vaginal/topical use in large amounts) is absorbed and inhibits CYP2C9 → markedly raised INR with warfarin; also raises sulfonylurea and phenytoin levels

## Pregnancy & lactation
Topical use safe.

## Viva points
- Miconazole oral gel + warfarin → bleeding (classic interaction)
- Useful in angular cheilitis (antifungal + antibacterial)

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.42 and ch.66 (Drug interactions); Khopkar ch.19. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
